name: OPQA
intro: OPQA（OpenAI-Proof Q&A）是 OpenAI 的内部研究与工程诊断评测，包含 20 个曾令重大项目至少延迟一天、且团队解决耗时超过一天的真实瓶颈。模型获得可访问代码与运行产物的容器，诊断性能回退、训练指标异常或隐蔽实现缺陷，并按 pass@1 评估；任务编写、参考答案、评分器和试验协议未公开。
build_method: 内部真实瓶颈筛选, 代码与运行证据容器封装（抽样、编写、参考答案及审核未披露）
metric: pass@1（评分器、量规与试验协议未披露）
task_type: Agent任务, 代码调试, 研究工程诊断
eval_feature: 内部评测, 代码执行环境
task_type_en: Agent task, code debugging, research engineering diagnosis
build_method_en: Internal Real-bottleneck Selection and Code/Run-evidence Container Packaging (sampling, authoring, references, and audit undisclosed)
eval_feature_en: Internal Evaluation, Containerized Code and Run Artifacts
intro_en: OPQA (OpenAI-Proof Q&A) is OpenAI's internal research and engineering diagnosis evaluation with 20 real bottlenecks that each delayed a major project by at least one day and took a team more than a day to resolve. Models receive a container with code access and run artifacts, diagnose performance regressions, anomalous training metrics, or subtle implementation bugs, and are evaluated with pass@1. Task authoring, reference answers, the grader, and the trial protocol are not public.
metric_en: pass@1 (grader, rubric, and trial protocol undisclosed)

drawio_review_note: Source-frozen review (reviewed_at=2026-07-18). The canonical official benchmark page is https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/gpt-5/opqa. It points to the revised GPT-5 system card at arXiv:2601.03267v2; the downloaded PDF has SHA-256 d40d91ae00d744f6f4d981750c8bd14be1bb217b236afe3b464e77405204b277 and the corresponding arXiv source archive has SHA-256 f422231814f299358c9fa813abde70a7b883e28cdb21b051130b680fdbf97bd6. OPQA appears in section 6.1.3.6 on page 42 of that frozen revision. The older first-party CDN artifact at https://cdn.openai.com/gpt-5-system-card.pdf has SHA-256 f9f9c72d08cba81dcbb189129119357c8c32eca4e0b16c813aca386aed6b0459 and places the materially equivalent OPQA paragraph in section 5.1.3.6 on page 39. The section number moved from 5.1.3.6 to 6.1.3.6 as the system card gained earlier material; that numbering change is not a change to the benchmark protocol. The fixed sources disclose exactly 20 internal OpenAI research and engineering bottlenecks. Each case caused at least a one-day delay to a major project and took more than a day for a team to solve; some affected large training runs or launches. The task is to diagnose and explain complex issues such as unexpected performance regressions, anomalous training metrics, and subtle implementation bugs. The model is given a container with code access and run artifacts; the system-card overview further identifies historical code, logs, and experiment data as available evidence. Each solution is graded using pass@1. In the frozen table, gpt-5-thinking has the highest listed OPQA result at 2%; this is a historical result in the cited card, not a current leaderboard or a ceiling on later systems. OPQA remains in-house. The official page and both fixed system-card artifacts expose no task payload, task examples, downloadable dataset, public repository, or public leaderboard, so openness remains in-house and has_leaderboard remains false. The sources do not disclose the source population or sampling frame, task-selection workflow beyond the stated consequence criterion, task authoring procedure, prompt text, reference answers, annotator or domain-expert roles, human audit, container assembly process, grader implementation, scoring rubric, acceptance threshold, trial protocol, repetition count, or aggregation details beyond pass@1. Put compactly, the system card does not disclose sampling, authoring, reference answers, grader, or trial protocol. These are evidence gaps, not permission to import procedures from adjacent evaluations. In particular, the GPT-5 system card describes other evaluations with human-written prompts, hidden unit tests, or repeated trials, but those statements are not attached to OPQA and are intentionally excluded from this graph. The source-stage diagram therefore has one solid disclosed path: consequential internal bottlenecks, the stated delay criterion, 20 in-house tasks, a container with code and run evidence, diagnosis and explanation, solution grading with pass@1, and the reported 2% result. Three dashed edges terminate at explicit boundaries for undisclosed construction, undisclosed grading, and lack of a public payload/repository/leaderboard. They do not depict inferred hidden stages. The source revision, section location, historical score, and openness limitations are encoded directly in labels so later rendering cannot silently turn an internal benchmark into a reproducible public dataset. Formal Draw.io, architecture sidecar, SVG, PNG, manifest, and deployed-site synchronization are deliberately outside this A11y source-stage review. Formal publication evidence [site-a11y-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 2167×465 (English) and 2165×465 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 2165×463 and 2163×463. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
